selection.text: A dose-response curve shows how the magnitude or nature of a biological or physiological response changes with the amount (dose) of a substance administered, typically plotted as response intensity versus dose. It reveals patterns such as baseline effects, maximal response, and sometimes inhibitory or decreased responses at higher doses. A peak at an intermediate dose can occur because beneficial or activating mechanisms may enhance the response at low‑to‑moderate doses, while higher doses trigger toxicity, receptor saturation, or negative feedback that reduces the observed response.
